children: You are building a letter-suggestion feature for a traditional telephone keypad. A user enters a short sequence of digits, and the feature must list every text sequence that those key presses could produce.

Each digit contributes exactly one letter. Keep the digits in their original order, and independently choose one mapped letter for each position. Return all resulting strings; their order in the returned list does not matter.
containing only the digits 2 through 9. Output: a list of all corresponding letter combinations.
Use this keypad mapping. The keys 0 and 1 do not supply any letters and are not part of a valid input:

examples.title: Example 1
examples.explanation: The first position chooses from a, b, c; the second chooses from d, e, f. Every pairing must be included, giving 3 × 3 = 9 strings.

examples.title: Example 2
examples.explanation: There is one position, so each letter on key 2 is one complete result.

examples.title: Example 3
examples.explanation: Keys 7 and 9 each have four letters. Their independent choices produce 16 strings.

children: The input contains between 1 and 4 digits, inclusive.
Every input character is one of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9.
Every result contains exactly one mapped letter per input position.
All combinations must be returned; list order is unrestricted.
